ctx.x: No, no, no. No. In the Bert Wheeler Theater it started at like -- we come back in -- from -- 1966

we came back from a tour with a jazz festival, which was the George Wein, you know. He had a monarchy with the jazz musicians. And he was going to get -- you see, Chuckles was working for this Gezler Gunther over there. See, I think he was working in Paris at that time.

Now, George's a conception -- I mean consideration, I'll say. He wanted to surprise Chuckles, you know, and the other tap dancers, you see, which was -- because Chuckles, he was like a big brother to them, you see. So, I don't want to be, you know, fraudulent. I'll say it again, see, because it was a -- would have been a nice thing to happen, you know. I mean the reunion of two partners, you know, that had -- was on the top and they was getting ready to -- see, reinstate themselves, you see, but in another…
